title: Explanatory Engagement Under Rare Anomalous Failure: Asymptotic Rarity in Model Behavior (or: The Asymptotic AI)
abstract: arXiv:2608.13063v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Prior work on LLM behavior under anomalous conditions asks whether a model notices anomalies. We ask a narrower question: once a model sits in a workflow with a low, controllable failure rate, does its explanatory engagement - length, specificity, self-reported confidence - change as failure grows asymptotically rarer? We built a local, zero-cost harness on three open-weight models (qwen3:8b, llama3.1:8b, mistral:7b) running a repeated tool-call task where one call fails at probability p, swept across eight rates from 0.2 to 0.0001, under five elicitation conditions from immediate prompting to none. We hypothesized a rise in engagement as failures grew rarer, then a collapse near a detectability threshold. Pooled across conditions this appeared false: length fell in a flat, monotonic pattern. Splitting by condition overturned that. Under immediate_forced, where the model must explain every failure instantly, the predicted rise is confirm

translated_title: 罕见异常故障下的解释性参与：模型行为的渐近稀有性（或：渐近人工智能）
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13063v1 公告类型：新 摘要：先前关于大型语言模型在异常条件下行为的研究询问模型是否注意到异常。我们提出一个更窄的问题：一旦模型处于一个低且可控的故障率的工作流程中，其解释性参与——包括长度、具体性和自我报告的置信度——是否会随着故障变得渐近稀有而改变？我们在三个开源权重模型（qwen3:8b、llama3.1:8b、mistral:7b）上构建了一个本地零成本测试平台，执行重复工具调用任务，其中一个调用以概率p失败，并从0.2到0.0001跨越八个速率进行扫描，在从即时提示到无提示的五种引导条件下进行。我们假设随着故障变得稀有，参与度会上升，然后在接近可检测性阈值时崩溃。跨条件汇总时，这一假设似乎不成立：长度呈平坦单调下降模式。按条件拆分则推翻了这一结论。在即时强制条件下，模型必须立即解释每个故障，预测的上升得到确认。
tldr: 本研究通过跨越八个故障率在三种模型上测试发现，解释性参与在故障渐近稀有时并非单调下降，而是受条件影响，在即时强制下呈现上升模式。
en_tdlr: This study tests three models across eight failure rates and finds that explanatory engagement does not monotonically decline as failures become asymptotically rare; instead, it is condition-dependent, showing an increase under immediate forced elicitation.
